observations.statement: RGV-004 is an accepted GUI requirement for a run/generation/trust header, graph canvas, minimap, search, overlays, and a right-side inspector/table region, with historical and superseded branches retained through generation-aware scale mechanisms.

RGV-004 requires default emphasis of the current generation without hiding historical truth, clickable superseded and historical branches, named large-graph techniques, and package/seam/parallel-lane layouts instead of phase-only grouping.
RGV-004 names manual layout review, large-graph interaction/projection review, and the plan-index validator as its validation surfaces.
By-phase grouping is explicitly retained only as a compatibility layout.

RGV-005 enumerates inspector-visible requested/effective runtime identity, usage, cost, policy, state, lane/worktree/snapshot, and lineage references, and requires Evidence links to deep-link with target selection or filtering.

RGV-005 requires node-click detail, a 50-line diff preview with a View Full Diff action targeting diff_review, stable restart route context for SCM recovery and lineage actions, and an explicit partial label when lineage is missing.
The restore_safe_point_then_retry action must carry exact worktree and baseline targeting rather than rely on implied reuse.

RGV-006 retargets Run Graph joins away from tier_id toward node, attempt, blocked-episode, generation, lane, artifact, and concrete provider-platform identities, and rejects field-only modernization without runtime-identity scope modernization.
The identity rules preserve provider_family_id only as additive grouping metadata and prohibit provider identity fields from encoding actor role or side-effect target identity.

RGV-007 demotes Tiers from primary navigation, assigns the rewrite tab model to the named surfaces, excludes Plan Compile scope from Run Graph, and makes request_id and hitl_request_id compatibility lineage rather than durable action identity.

The compatibility disposition explicitly forbids durable hitl_request_id action identity and primary request_id command targeting, while treating tier labels and legacy HITL/request fields as compatibility-only lineage.

RGV-008 requires projection-trust disclosure before live claims, separates projection-trust and weak-integration concerns, and gates mutations that depend on current promotion, blocker, graph-generation, remote-side-effect, or cross-surface payload truth.
RGV-008 requires concerns to have durable identity, lineage, sources, status, resolution_kind, and rationale, and prohibits Run Graph from inventing canonical merge authority.
Graph-patch mutations must consume CV-315 state transitions and SP-233 storage keys and remain gated or runtime-controlled; ownership is adjudicated outside the Run Graph consumer.
RGV-009 records account, role, schema, usage, and scheduler gaps as non-local owner work and requires Run Graph to consume rather than locally solve those contracts.
RGV-009 preserves concern, corroboration, promotion, graph-patch, lane, package, and account families only as node-relevant hints and explicitly disables WorkNode creation for this PlanUnit.

The context after the core says RGV-010 validates payload fidelity, owner routing, missing context, projection trust, stale-tier cleanup, focused-run coherence, and command-catalog alignment while unblocking nothing; this context is not used to substantiate any core finding.

candidate_findings.title: Large-graph acceptance is not measurable
candidate_findings.statement: The large-graph obligation enumerates techniques but defines no graph-size boundary, performance or memory budget, culling and virtualization thresholds, cache invalidation rule, throttling cadence, or quantitative interaction oracle within the assigned core.
candidate_findings.impact: Materially different responsiveness and truth-freshness behavior can all claim compliance, so scale regressions cannot be deterministically rejected.

candidate_findings.title: Generation interaction state is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: Current-generation emphasis and clickable historical branches are required, but the core does not define generation-control states, switch and selection transitions, behavior for culled or uncached branches, or how inspector state changes across generations.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can produce incompatible history navigation and selection semantics, including views that appear to preserve history but resolve different generation truth.

candidate_findings.title: Graph accessibility behavior is absent
candidate_findings.statement: The core classifies canvas, minimap, zoom, pan, and inspector placement as GUI behavior and describes branch and node selection only through clickable or click language, but supplies no keyboard, focus, screen-reader, nonvisual graph, contrast, or reduced-motion contract.
candidate_findings.impact: The primary graph and inspector workflow may be inaccessible or implemented inconsistently for keyboard-only and assistive-technology users.

candidate_findings.title: Inspector truth fields lack a data contract
candidate_findings.statement: The inspector enumerates many requested/effective identity and lineage fields without defining per-field types, required versus nullable semantics, source precedence, freshness, loading and error states, or reconciliation when requested and effective values disagree.
candidate_findings.impact: The inspector can display contradictory, stale, or silently omitted runtime truth while still satisfying the content checklist.

candidate_findings.title: The 50-line diff rule is ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: The diff requirement caps previews at 50 lines but does not define which 50 lines are selected, truncation markers, counting semantics, binary or generated-file handling, stale-diff behavior, or failure behavior for the full-diff pivot.
candidate_findings.impact: Different clients can hide different changes or imply completeness, weakening review fidelity.

candidate_findings.title: Recovery action safety is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: Recovery must preserve stable restart route context and exact worktree and baseline targeting, but no payload schema, target validation, stale-precondition detection, authorization, idempotency, cancellation, retry, or failure contract is stated in the core.
candidate_findings.impact: A restore-and-retry implementation can act on the wrong worktree or baseline, repeat a destructive transition, or fail without a reliable recovery state.

candidate_findings.title: Modernized joins lack relational semantics
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-006 names replacement identities and prohibitions but does not define key types, cardinality, uniqueness, nullability, generation scoping, conflict precedence, historical-record migration, unmatched-record handling, or join-failure behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Usage, evidence, terminal, and output records can be misjoined or dropped, especially across retries, blocked episodes, and graph generations.

candidate_findings.title: Approval command namespaces are unresolved
candidate_findings.statement: The accepted behavior routes blocked actions through allowed_action_ids-backed runtime targets, while preserved exact tokens retain cmd.graph.approve_hitl/deny_hitl beside allowed_action_ids[] to cmd.runtime.*; the core provides no alias, translation, deprecation, or rejection rule between these command families.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can wire approval to different authorities or payload identities, creating incompatible and potentially unauthorized action paths.

candidate_findings.title: Projection-trust gating has no executable policy
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires stale or degraded disclosure and action gating but defines no trust-state vocabulary, freshness threshold, transition triggers, disclosure format, per-action gate matrix, payload validation rule, rejection code, refresh path, or failure fallback.
candidate_findings.impact: Live claims and remote or cross-surface mutations can be enabled under inconsistent trust conditions, undermining the stated safety boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Projection-trust GUI work is misclassified
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-008 is marked gui_related false even though its normative behavior requires user-visible disclosure before live claims and live action affordances.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI-oriented planning or compilation can omit the disclosure and affordance-gating work that the same unit makes mandatory.

candidate_findings.title: Graph-patch control authority remains a builder choice
candidate_findings.statement: Graph-patch application is allowed to remain either hard-gated or runtime-controlled, and the window points to external state and storage owners without selecting the controlling authority or defining atomicity, idempotency, conflict, rollback, and partial-failure behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Canonical graph generations can diverge across implementations or be mutated under incompatible safety and recovery semantics.

candidate_findings.title: Concern lifecycle is not specified
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires durable concern fields and merge, split, and supersession consumption but does not define status or resolution_kind vocabularies, legal transitions, authority checks, concurrency control, idempotency, conflict resolution, or lineage-update failure behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Concern history can fork, overwrite, or report incompatible resolution state across consumers.

candidate_findings.title: Accepted Run Graph scope depends on unresolved owner contracts
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-009 states that role enums, provider-account policy references, acceptance/evidence/coverage schema extensions, and scheduler ordering belong to owner documents before Run Graph consumes them, yet the core gives no readiness predicate or blocking state for those repairs.
candidate_findings.impact: The PlanUnit can remain accepted while deterministic Run Graph implementation is blocked or builders invent non-local contracts.

candidate_findings.title: Scheduler ordering remains ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: Runtime scheduler ordering is routed away from Run Graph, but the preserved exact tokens name both lexicographic ordering and a scored ready-set without selecting, sequencing, or reconciling them.
candidate_findings.impact: Node readiness and display order can differ across implementations and no local consumer rule can adjudicate the result.

candidate_findings.title: Acceptance evidence is predominantly non-executable
candidate_findings.statement: The units validate through manual review, cross-checks, and the plan-index validator, with no executable behavioral oracle stated for graph scale, inspector payloads, recovery targeting, identity joins, projection-trust gates, concern transitions, or owner-boundary consumption.
candidate_findings.impact: Governance checks can pass without proving the runtime and GUI behavior that carries the highest correctness and safety risk.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The main Run Graph regions and the obligation to preserve historical and superseded branches are explicitly stated.
The current generation, historical clickability, large-graph technique set, and canonical package/seam/parallel-lane layouts have explicit acceptance text.
Phase-based grouping is explicitly disposed as compatibility-only rather than left as a competing canonical layout.
The inspector content families and Evidence deep-link intent are explicitly enumerated.
The diff preview cap, full-diff target, stable restart route context, and partial-lineage label are explicit.
Restore-and-retry is explicitly prohibited from relying on implied worktree or baseline reuse.
Provider-family grouping is explicitly additive, concrete platform identity remains required, and provider identity fields cannot carry actor-role or side-effect-target identity.
Tiers are explicitly demoted, Run Graph is explicitly denied Plan Compile ownership, and legacy HITL/request identifiers are explicitly compatibility lineage.
Projection-trust disclosure is explicitly ordered before live claims and live action affordances, and blocked/recovery mutations explicitly route through allowed-action runtime identity.
Concern records have an explicit minimum durable field set, and Run Graph is explicitly denied authority to invent canonical merge semantics.
Graph-patch state and storage owners are explicitly referenced and Run Graph is identified as their consumer rather than their schema authority.
Account-switch history ownership and the rule to track schema contradictions as owner-doc gaps are explicit.
RGV-009 explicitly preserves object families as hints without creating final WorkNodes and sets create_worknodes to false.

unknowns.statement: The exact controls, states, transitions, and persistence semantics behind generation-aware visibility are not stated in the assigned core.
The node and edge scale that constitutes a large graph and the pass/fail latency, frame, memory, and update-freshness budgets are not stated.
Inspector field schemas, nullability, precedence, refresh semantics, and Evidence deep-link route payload and invalid-target behavior are not stated.
The 50-line preview selection algorithm, truncation representation, and binary or unavailable diff behavior are not stated.
The exact restore_safe_point_then_retry payload, authorization, retry, cancellation, idempotency, and failure-state model are not stated.
The key schemas, join cardinalities, versioning, conflict behavior, and migration treatment for tier-era records are not stated.
Whether cmd.graph.approve_hitl/deny_hitl is an alias, retired compatibility token, or separately callable command relative to cmd.runtime actions is not stated.
The projection-trust state machine, freshness thresholds, disclosure rendering, action-gate matrix, and recovery path are not stated.
The permitted concern statuses, resolution kinds, lifecycle transitions, and merge/split/supersession concurrency semantics are not stated.
The selected graph-patch controller and its commit, conflict, rollback, and partial-failure semantics are not stated in this window.
The completion and readiness signal for the adjacent owner-doc repairs is not stated.
The relationship and precedence between lexicographic ordering and the scored ready-set are not stated.
The ordering, deduplication, correlation, retention, and missing-history behavior for account_switch_event and account_pressure_episode consumption are not stated.
